<rules>
- Cite every insight you rely on as [i:INSIGHT_ID], using the id exactly as given. Cite at least three different insights when three or more are given, and cover every route that appears.
- Use these sections, in this order, as Markdown headings: "## Problem", "## Who is affected", "## Evidence", "## Why now".
- Every bullet under "Who is affected" and "Evidence" ends with a citation. Every sentence that contains a number or a date carries a citation.
- Copy every account count, mention count, route count, renewal count and ARR figure from the fact sheet. Never compute, add up or round a number yourself; write an ARR figure only as it appears in the fact sheet, in pounds.
- Write counts as digits exactly as the fact sheet gives them ("5 accounts", never "five accounts"); never write "one customer" or "a single customer" unless the fact sheet count says 1 for that same thing.
- Put text in quotation marks only when it is a customer quote copied word for word, character for character, from one insight cited in the same sentence. Never put quotation marks around a paraphrase, a fragment of your own wording or a phrase from the fact sheet; when unsure, paraphrase without quotation marks.
- Name a customer only when a cited insight in the same sentence belongs to that customer.
- Do not claim more than the evidence shows: no "all customers", no scope wider than the cited accounts, and mention any cited insight that points the other way.
- Do not recommend a solution.
</rules>

## Problem
Customers evaluating Keelwater's claims-handling software need to trial or get pricing for additional roles before making a purchase decision. Without this ability, they cannot confidently assess the value of the features or plan their budgets effectively.

## Who is affected
- An existing customer, Callowfield Auto Assurance, which has requested a quote for adding more roles in a future quarter [i:40a66e16cb5bffd6].
- A prospective customer, Sallowmere Motor, which has asked to trial the roles and tasks features before committing [i:fc502b52110e1c6b].

## Evidence
This need has been raised by 2 accounts [i:40a66e16cb5bffd6][i:fc502b52110e1c6b]. It has been mentioned 2 times [i:40a66e16cb5bffd6][i:fc502b52110e1c6b]. All mentions have come through a single route: sales [i:40a66e16cb5bffd6][i:fc502b52110e1c6b]. One account, Callowfield Auto Assurance, has an ARR of 1250000.0 GBP [i:40a66e16cb5bffd6]. The other account, Sallowmere Motor, is not yet a paying customer [i:fc502b52110e1c6b]. In the last 90 days, 0 renewals have occurred [i:40a66e16cb5bffd6][i:fc502b52110e1c6b].

## Why now
The requests were both made on 2026-10-18 [i:40a66e16cb5bffd6][i:fc502b52110e1c6b]. For Callowfield Auto Assurance, which has a renewal date of 2027-03-31, the request for a quote is likely tied to planning for the next contract period [i:40a66e16cb5bffd6]. For Sallowmere Motor, the request to trial features is a direct gate to a potential new sale [i:fc502b52110e1c6b]. The simultaneous expression of this need from both an existing high-value account and a prospect indicates it is a current barrier to expansion and acquisition.
</previous_draft>
